doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Opening and teaching years in public school and UConn
summary: Rowe opens the filmed interview; Masso counts eleven years in public school and seven at UConn as high school music director and teacher trainer.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive, and I’m pleased to have George Masso as my guest here in Aspen, Colorado, jazz trombonist and educator. And so, welcome.
You say you taught public school for eighteen years?

Well public school for eleven years, and then seven years at the University of Connecticut, where I was doing most of the work at the high school, which at that time was a part of the Department of Education. I was Music Director there at the high school, E.O. Smith School to be specific, and I also was involved in teacher training for the university, the music ed majors.
